subject: English
passage: Amira Yusuf's 1988 documentary film Border Stories explores immigration experiences through a series of personal interviews—interviews that Yusuf filmed using an innovative handheld camera technique. During a recent film festival screening, some audience members commented that they found the documentary's handheld style disorienting and its portrayal of family dynamics outdated. The festival director, however, noted that the film employs cutting-edge editing techniques and examines social issues that remain pressing today, suggesting that Border Stories ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: has more to say about family dynamics than other documentaries from the same era.
choices.B: is easier to follow than many contemporary documentaries that focus on immigration.
choices.C: is more relevant to contemporary audiences than it may seem at first.
choices.D: is best appreciated when viewed using the original handheld camera equipment.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of Amira Yusuf's 1988 documentary Border Stories. The text states that the documentary consists of personal interviews filmed using an innovative handheld technique—a style that some audience members at a festival screening found disorienting. According to the text, those viewers also found the documentary's portrayal of family dynamics to be outdated. In response to the audience's concerns, the festival director emphasized the film's continued relevance: it employs cutting-edge editing and examines issues that remain pressing today. This, in turn, suggests that Border Stories is more relevant to contemporary audiences than it may initially seem.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because the festival director's response to the audience only mentions Border Stories; it doesn't compare the documentary to others from the same era.
